note_on_this_round: ONE GAP: `W1-F10-r12-CRITIC` — *the crowd breathes and there are still fourteen people in it*. 14 rendered bodies for 408 records, 93 identical pairs within 15 m, 3 build bands of 5. This round is geometry, not pose: an AGE axis the registry never had, twelve new archetypes, race-scoped pools, and three proportion cuts. The rendered body count is 14 -> 72 and the count is the least interesting number in the round; the discriminators that try to prove it worthless are the point.
what_i_could_not_do: **E1 STILL FAILS, AND I AM NOT THE ONE WHO CAN CLOSE IT.** The rendered arm passes with margin — 72 distinct bodies for 408 records, one per 5.67 against a bar of one per 12, largest bucket `sax.stooped-elder~wiry` at 13 = 3.19% against a 40 ceiling. But `RI-VIS10` E1 as the r9 critic amended it requires BOTH arms, and the `actor` arm is unchanged at **32 distinct `actor` values with `townsman` at 97 = 23.8%**. `actor` is a DIALOGUE key, not a visual one — read this turn: `game/src/render/actor.js` never mentions it, while `character/converse.js:311,314,655,687` and `sim/quest/topic-supply.js:308` select lines by it and `game/data/dialogue/greetings/00-priority-classes.json` and `topics/00-roots.json` key on it. Splitting `townsman` into three actor classes to move a VISUAL count would silently change which greeting 97 people speak and would be scored by `tools/dialogue/root-coverage.mjs`. **I declined to trade a measured dialogue requirement for a visual one and I fail E1 closed.** The r9 amendment's own words are the argument — *'`actor` reaches the simulation and never reaches the camera; a census over it is counting a column no viewer can see'* — and the r12 critic's own remedy scopes its DONE condition to the rendered arm alone. This is a corpus finding for a critic, not a bar for a builder to rewrite (S59).

**E4 IS BETTER AND STILL FAILS: 93 identical pairs within 15 m -> 28.** The bar is 0 and the remedy asked for < 3. I can show why the remaining 28 are not a body-pool problem, and the argument is arithmetic rather than rhetoric: pairs fall roughly as 1/pool, so 28 -> under 3 needs the pool to go from 72 to about 400 — and at 400 bodies on ONE skeleton with proportion-only variation, the closest pair's silhouette IoU necessarily approaches 1.0, which is the C2 clause I already fail at 0.9905. **E4 at zero and C2's no-pair->=0.93 are jointly unsatisfiable by any pool-based design on a fixed skeleton, and that is a finding about the item, not an excuse.** The item's own E4 tuple is `(actor, head, garment, scale)` — and `garment` is D1, which scores 0 because the garment vocabulary does not exist, while `scale` is `height_scale`, which `renderer.js:801` already reads and which is **1.000 on all 408 records**. The residual is a WARDROBE and a STATURE problem and both live outside this file.

**I DELIBERATELY DID NOT USE A SCALE AXIS, AND A READER SHOULD DECIDE WHETHER THAT WAS RIGHT.** Per-individual stature is the single cheapest visible crowd cue and it would have taken E4 most of the way down. I refused it because it is the one change that `RI-VIS10` C2's height-normalised 120 px masks CANNOT see and that `variantKey` does not hash — i.e. the one axis no discriminator in this item can refuse — and because the brief's own trap is *'fourteen bodies becoming forty by permuting a scale factor'*. It is also a DATA field (`height_scale` in `game/data/npcs/`) owned by whoever owns that data, and applying it in the render layer would make the renderer the authority on a simulation field. **If a critic rules that reasoning too pure, the fix is one field on 408 records and it is the highest-value single step left in this item.**

**B1, C4 and D4 not run — no fresh judge (rule 0e), sixth verdict for B1.** A builder cannot spawn one; `create_session` is approval-gated and rule 0 forbids it. B1 is one of the four checks blocking the 7-8 band and I could not reach it.

**D5 not run and B2 / B4 / D3 not re-derived.** D5 (garment wear) has never been measured by anybody and I did not fix that; B2 (6 of 10), B4 (1 of 7) and D3 (2 of 8) are carried from r10 and I re-derived none of them. **My twelve new archetype rows inherit whatever B2/B4/D3 score the base bodies had** — they add no facial landmark and no material that was not already there, so the honest expectation is that those three numbers are unchanged and I did not confirm it.

**C3's attribution arm (b2-iii) is CARRIED, not re-run.** I measured (a), (b1), (b2-i) and (b2-ii) live this turn. (b2-iii) — >= 60% of changed pixels inside drawn NPCs' screen boxes at >= 3x enrichment — is the r12 critic's own measurement on the r12 tree (82.28-85.66% inside boxes covering 9.09-9.36%), and I did not re-shoot it. The motion code is untouched by this round, which is a reason to expect it holds and is not a measurement.

**THE BUDGET CLAUSE IS NOT CLOSED AS WRITTEN, for the third round running, and I did not retry the thing that has now failed five times.** `HAZARDS §29` and the r12 critic both record that a SwiftShader frame-time pair cannot answer this clause at any n this box will give: a frame costs ~10 s and the term under test is four stance solves. **What I can say from the code and did check: this round adds NO per-frame work at all.** `buildSkeleton` already runs once per actor (`ensureBuilt` (`actor.js:2699`, `if (A.built) return A.built` at :2701) returns the cached body on every later call), so 408 actors already built 408 geometries before this round; widening the pool changes WHICH numbers are used, not how many builds happen. The composed specs are memoised in `_COMPOSED`, bounded by rows x 3. `addCharacterPosture` is 4 array adds on the 73 of 408 people who carry a stoop, inside a solve that already ran. **That is an argument, not a number, and the clause asks for a number.**

**THE r12 SELF-TEST'S ARM 2 IS RED ON THIS TREE AND I LEFT IT RED.** `f10-r12-crowd-motion.mjs --self-test` reports 268 of 408 rows mismatched against round 11's banked stance table. I did not edit that tool: a previous round's instrument going red on a later tree is evidence, and rewriting it deletes the evidence. **I diagnosed it instead and the diagnosis is in `f10-r13-stance-preservation.mjs`** — that arm reads every row on ONE reused probe actor per family (`makeProbeActor` at :165, renamed per row by `readAt` at :179), which was sound while the body could not reach the pose and is not sound now. Read on each person's OWN body, as `syncNPCs` builds them: **335 of 408 reproduce byte for byte, the 73 that differ are EXACTLY the 73 who carry a stoop, and with the age axis neutralised the control returns 408 of 408.** A critic should still treat that red as owed a fix by whoever next touches that tool.
**LILMOTH, NOT HELSTROM — fifth verdict running.** Every live number here is the r10 critic's Lilmoth stand. Helstrom's 78 people are covered offline at 100% and have never been photographed.
**NO APPEARANCE CLAIM.** SwiftShader, `W1-30-EVIDENCE §4`. My frames establish what is in shot, which bodies are drawn and whether they differ in outline — nothing about how anything looks.
headline: 14 rendered bodies -> 72, and every discriminator I could build says they are 72 different shapes rather than 72 names: 72 distinct structural keys for 72 names (no free names), a null control that collapses the same roster back to 24 bodies and 69 adjacency pairs, C1 held at 72 of 72 inside the 7.0-8.0 band, and the whole difference from round 11's 408 stands isolated to the 73 people who carry the new age axis. E1's rendered arm, E3 and E5 move to pass and D2 is scored for the first time in four verdicts; E1 overall and E4 still fail and I say why.

findings.inspected: `SKILL.md` and `grimoire/character/structure_decomposition.md`, both fetched at the pin and read this turn. Round 12 declined it and flagged it as still live for the geometry half; this round IS the geometry half, so I made my own call and it is a different one.
findings.decisive_reason: ITS LAYER ONTOLOGY IS A REAL CHECK AND I APPLIED IT; ITS PIPELINE IS NOT ADOPTABLE HERE. `structure_decomposition.md`'s nine layers turn on one test — *'does this part cross a joint?'* — with L3 (single-bone isolates, forced to weight (1,0,0,0)) and L4 (cross-joint shells, spatial weights) as the two answers. I ran my new geometry through it before believing it: the dorsal mass crosses no joint and is bound to `spine_02` alone (L3-shaped, correct); the girdle-roll tube DOES cross the shoulder and is therefore emitted with a real blend (`B.cloth.tube(..., armI2, clavI2, 0.5, ...)`) rather than pinned. Its L-1 'Proportion Scaffold' — a head-unit system every part is clamped into — is the same idea `actor.js`'s `TARGET_EXTENT` head solve already implements independently, and reading it is what made me bound the cut layer's `head` axis to +/-3% instead of guessing. **No source copied**, which is what `concept-only` permits. What I did NOT take: its build method is SDF smooth-union into marching cubes for the core volume, which would produce a second body plan whose surface is not the skinned tube-and-ellipsoid surface `hitgeometry.json`'s capsules are segments of — a second authority, which IMPLEMENTATION-LEADS says needs an explicit roadmap ruling, in exchange for nothing this gap asked for. This round adds no new mesh; it varies the numbers an existing parametric body is built from.

the_change_in_three_parts.1_an_age_axis_the_registry_never_had: `lib/rigs.js:MORPH_KEYS` gains `stoop`, neutral **0** rather than 1 because it is a curvature and not a multiplier — so `resolveMorph` leaves every pre-round-13 row bit-identical. It has TWO consumers and both are required: geometry (a dorsal mass over the upper spine plus a forward girdle roll, in `buildSkeleton`, bound to bones that already own those regions, no bone offset moved) and posture (`addCharacterPosture`, a persistent forward curvature added into the stance layer `poseStatic` already solves, with 0.55 of the trunk's pitch returned at the neck so the eyeline stays up). the_change_in_three_parts.3_race_scoped_pools_and_three_cuts: `RACE_POOL` scopes the archetype pool by race — naga, imperial, dunmer, nord, breton and khajiit each draw rows another race there does not, which is what E5 asks for and what `artFamilyForRace` alone (twelve race strings onto two body plans) could never give. `renderer.js:syncNPCs` passes `n.race` as `makeRiggedActor`'s fifth argument; that one line is the whole wiring. Three published cuts — `wiry`, `asbuilt` (the archetype exactly as authored, so a third of the crowd keeps the body it had and nothing shipped is lost), `thickset` — multiply six axes each. The identity stamped on the meshes is `<archetype>~<cut>`. Both draws are FNV-1a over differently prefixed keys of `group.name`, so they are independent and stable per person.

job_1_the_one_gap_fourteen_bodies.the_child_band_ruling: E3's fifth band is `child` and the remedy asked for one at `build < 0.70`. **I did not build it, on purpose, and this is a ruling a critic may overturn in one line.** (a) `lib/rigs.js` forbids bone lengths as a variant axis because `hitgeometry.json` declares every hurtbox as a segment OF a bone — so a `build 0.65` figure is an adult-height skeleton with thin limbs, which reads as a starved adult and not as a child. (b) A real child's canon of proportion is 5-6 heads; `RI-VIS10` C1 hard-fails outside 6.0-8.5, so **a genuine child cannot pass C1 as the item is written**. E3 needs 4 of 5 and I delivered 4 of 5 without inventing the one that would have to lie. **The honest route to a child is a second skeleton and a per-age C1 band, which is a piece of work and not a morph value.** Overturned if a critic rules children in scope for F10 at all.

job_3_the_four_people_six_km_out_to_sea.why_they_were_at_sea_and_not_hidden_like: two separate mechanisms, and this is the difference from the 29 round 12 diagnosed. **(1) Position:** 15 of the 16 posts carry coordinates 5.1-9.7 km from the settlement the record itself names — the five Lilmoth ones sit at x 4891-4912, z -589 to -596, against Lilmoth's own centre at (2766.5, 5027.5) in `game/data/world/pois.json`. Only `captain-oreem` (archon, 22.3 m from centre) is right. **(2) Visibility:** `sim/npc.js:applyPresence` sets `visible = present`, and for a record with `at: null` and a `post.settlement`, present means *the player is outdoors*. So these people are correctly VISIBLE and incorrectly PLACED — the exact inverse of the 29 at the origin, who are correctly placed in an interior frame and correctly hidden.
job_3_the_four_people_six_km_out_to_sea.and_they_steal_four_people_from_two_othe: `engine.js:populateSettlement` skips a record whose id is already spawned (`if (this.sim.findNPC(rec.id)) continue`). Because the witness copies name `lilmoth` while the real records name `archon` and `gideon`, populating Lilmoth spawns the witness copy first and the real record is then blocked. Four people were therefore missing from Archon and Gideon as well as standing in the Topal.
